notes.A: Conventional SaaS layout with the Team card and table column highlighted, so the plans, prices and orange call to action are found instantly, but it looks like a template.
notes.B: Tidy, well-aligned page with a clear toggle, green call to action buttons and a closing call to action band, though it reads as a generic SaaS template and repeats the tagline.
notes.C: Condensed editorial headline, ruled hairlines and bold prices give it a ledger-like character while keeping plans, table and FAQ clean on both desktop and phone.
notes.D: Warm, full-width plan rows with big prices and a clear header button work well, but the first screen shows only one and a half plans and the phone cards leave awkward gaps.
notes.E: Serif headings, green palette and a statement-to-ledger illustration feel trustworthy and calm for bookkeepers, with solid structure, though prices sit half below the first screen.
notes.F: Clean and correct but the most generic page, with no call to action in the first screen or header and little character.
notes.G: Distinctive serif type and double-underlined prices suit an accounting product, but the mobile comparison table breaks words mid-word and the call to action only appears lower in the cards.
notes.H: Archival ledger photos and a bento hero look striking but are decoration that pushes prices out of the first screen, and the mobile footer wordmark is broken into scattered letters.
notes.I: Three prices and their buttons sit in the first screen as horizontal rows, and the comparison, stat strip and FAQ are crisp, restrained and well-spaced on phone.
notes.J: Huge two-tone type and pastel blocks are bold and memorable, but the plans fall below the first screen, the staggered cards look unsteady and the low-contrast call to action bars are weak.
